Everything is perfect, from trying to automate production and min-maxing the harvest, to simply speaking with valley's people and understand their personality. There are times that I just boot the game, and fish for 2 hours straight. 
If that isn't enough, the modding community is such bless, with mods such as SV Expanded, that, even if you achieve perfection in vanilla, you still have plenty to do, if you're willing to get into modding.
To sum it up, this game is a genuine masterpiece.

I'm surprised I never wrote a review for this game.

I could just write "It's great. Buy it now." and that alone would be a valid review, but I'll go just a little further.

If you've ever played the persona games and enjoyed making the most out of your time or wanted to be rewarded for planning ahead, this game is definitely for you. There may be some things that you can't plan for on your first playthrough until you find out they exist, but odds are you'll eventually want to start a new farm anyways, whether it be to try out different stuff, be more efficient, or check out something you may have missed the first time. 

HOWEVER, if you'd say you're more intrinsically motivated and do stuff just for the sake of it, that's fun too! I find the game intrinsically fun and it's made the game very replayable as a result. Unlike real life, doing just about ANYTHING can generate you money. Not all money-making methods are created equally of course, but you have options nonetheless.

The music and atmosphere in this game is great too. The winter themes specifically are my favorites.

There's also mod support, so you can make the game more fun by getting a modded farm layout, new NPCs, QoL mods, new crops, new areas, resprite characters, etc.

Try the game out sometime, even if none of this may have sounded cool to you. There's quite a bit to do in this game with plenty of polish, and I recommend not playing with the wiki or anything until later and you've found yourself wanting to go beyond what you've already figured out. If that never happens and you just end up mining 24/7 because you find it funner than anything else, that's cool too!

Unfortunately I don't find myself having the time to write as good of a review as I'd like, but hopefully this will do.

In short, this game is well worth the money for offering a cozy farming gameplay, with a lot of optional challenges and assets that you can utilize to create your ideal country life.

As for a lengthy review however, i would like to mention about my first exposure to this game. It was around 2020 when i was watching a youtuber who playthrough of minecraft modpacks. Suddenly one day, he posted a video series about Stardew Valley. Seeing something far different from the usual contents that the youtuber made, i was pretty hooked and then watched the series myself. The vibe of the game felt so fun for me, someone who at the time still find farming flash games to pass the time, with its top-down perspective and colorful design. Sadly however, the series only lasted until summer yr 1, and the youtuber himself moved back to doing minecraft modpacks. Feeling a bit upset that i couldn't be able to see more about the game itself, and mind you, i myself back then didn't even know Steam's existence, which further makes me want to try the game myself.

Fast forward to 2022, i finally get myself a PC, and i get to know some "unusual ways" to "install" games onto my PC, so i tried to get Stardew Valley onto my desktop as quick as possible. Even though 2 years have passed, my experience with the game itself doesn't change at all. The vibrant color design, the cozy feeling of a country side farm, which further fuels my excitement to finally get an experience of the game. First time getting into the game, it was a bit tough for me to understand the story and how some buttons work. But by utilizing my experience from watching the video series, i did manage to plant some parsnips and greet all the villagers. Fast forward to day 3, i finally set my foot to the shore to meet the fisherman, and he gave me a fishing pole. And oh boy, i spent so many days fishing for extra cash. Many people in the community may consider the fishing minigame to be hard, but that's the thing that hooked me, the pain of trying to get a catfish at lvl 1 fishing was so worth it. After a while, i finally checked the mailbox after countless days of fishing, just to see that the very first event of spring, the egg hunt has already passed away. i was a bit upset over that fact, so i went to the central town to check the calendar if there're any other events coming up and slapped straight to my face was the community center cutscene with mayor himself. We went inside to see how ruined the community center was, and the mayor asked me to help repairing the community center, else he was gonna sell it to a nearby establishment. I thought to myself, "guess i should check this out after-" and right at that moment, a apple-looking creature appeared behind the mayor. My character was shocked, and so do I. Looking at how the mayor said i was probably sick or something made me so annoyed, since the creature is literally right behind him all the time, made me yelling "IT IS BEHIND YOU!!!" so loud that my mom came to check what i was doing. After some explanation to my mom, i went back to the game and checked around the community center, which was when i found a tablet that was written in whatever language that i couldnt even google translate it. After that, i went out of the community center and check the calendar to see the next event is the flower dance, which is in the 24th, and it was the 19th when i checked the calendar, so i went back to the beach to enjoy my past time with my fishing pole. The very next day, when i was about to do another fishing trip, i saw the the mail notification. I went to check it to see a letter from a wizard wanting to meet me at his hut in the forest. So instead of going to the beach, i went to the forest to check on him, The wizard was a bit rude to me, and gave me a strange brew that made me hallucinate a bunch of trees here and there. But after all that, he told me i could understand the tablet. Leaving the hut, i made my way to the community center to check the tablet again, and indeed i could read it now. The first tablet had a bundle that requires spring forageables, which i already have some at home, so i fulfilled the first bundle to unlock the next one. One by one, i get to see myself skipping so many aspects of the game. First was farming, i barely planted anything other than the first parsnips the mayor left for me to begin my farm. Second is mining, i wasnt paying attention that there is a mine i could work on. But hey, i left those all behind, because i liked fishing more than anything at the point. I  then again fished until the 24th of spring, where i participated my very first event. Seeing the villagers anticipating such a gorgeous event with beautiful flowers and happy dancing couples was fun, though it was sad that i couldnt get anyone to dance with me, since i spent all my time fishing, meaning my relationship with everything was low, aside from the fisherman himself, since i gave him some of my catches whenever he passes by. And after that event ended, i had to end my playthrough right there due to some complications within my family.

Now, moving to the year 2026, being in college with some free time and money i can spend for hobbies, i recall of Stardew Valley, so i grabbed the game on Steam when a sale happens. Even though i can buy the game and play it for however long i want, one thing that i miss having is the carefree mindset i had back in the day, to spend so much time fishing without a care of other aspects. Even though i missed the feeling, i still think that by reaching perfection and finishing the achievement tab, i have fulfilled my desire to experience the game fully back in the day.

All and all, grab the game and enjoy a cozy farming experience. 🏠
